object_description: six-storey slab aligned to the park with a street-side plinth and a transverse gymnasium
design_condition: the school is aligned with the park while a plinth takes up the volumetric occupation along the street and a transverse gymnasium completes the composition at the height of the planned high-rise base

positive: The special position of school buildings as free-standing public institutions is convincingly derived
The proposal remains one of the few that opens up the main side of the school to the park
The plinth along the street takes up the volumetric occupation set by the design plan
The transverse gymnasium relates in height to the base of the planned high-rise
The central break area between classroom wing and gymnasium is staggered in height
Each level is characterised differently by materials, planting and possible uses
The clear positioning of entrance and forecourt to the park is welcomed in principle
The arrangement of the various break areas creates good zoning and a variety of uses
The internal logic of the school develops naturally from the clear urban setting
A sequence of two-storey residential courtyards alternately opens to park or schoolyard
The efficiently organised floor plan gains spatial diversity from this sequence
A centrally located staircase sculpture links the two-storey care areas
These merge into the more intimate single-storey clusters
negative: The retaining wall at the staircase extends the building like an attached plinth
It draws the image of the paved square far into the park, which is considered unfortunate
The small pocket park in the south appears suspended
Its function is incomprehensible, being hard to reach and unfavourably positioned in the urban fabric
The staircase open across all floors is viewed critically in terms of acoustic pollution
